excerpt: How to set a PIN, pattern, or fingerprint on a phone, lock a laptop when you step away, and choose how quickly each one locks itself.

body.text: This lesson teaches you to lock a phone and a laptop so a stranger cannot open them. You will set a PIN or a pattern, turn on a fingerprint, and make the machine lock itself when you walk away. It takes ten minutes and protects everything else in these lessons.
A lock screen is a door between the world and your messages, photos, and accounts. It is the cheapest security you will ever set up, and every phone and laptop already has one.
Before you start

items: The phone or laptop, charged.
A PIN you can remember, not one written on the back of the phone.
About fifteen minutes.

body.text: Set the phone lock

items: Open Settings, then Security, or Lock screen on Samsung phones.
Choose Screen lock type and pick PIN, which is the most reliable.
Use six digits rather than four, and avoid your birth year.
Do not use 1234, 0000, or the last four digits of your number.
Add a fingerprint if the phone has a reader, as a faster way in.
Choose how long the phone waits before locking: thirty seconds is a good balance.

body.text: You will see the lock screen appear with a keypad and the time at the top. After you unlock twice, the phone stops asking for a full sign-in for a while, which is normal.

body.alt: A phone lock screen showing a PIN keypad.
body.caption: Six digits and a fingerprint. The keypad appears every time the screen wakes, before anything else is visible.

body.text: It looks like a lock screen only stops somebody browsing your photos. It also stops them opening your email, resetting a password, and seeing the codes that arrive by text.
A pattern is weaker than a PIN
Patterns are quick to draw and quick to copy from a smudge on the glass. A PIN is the better choice for a phone that travels.

items: If you prefer a pattern, turn off the visible lines, which give it away.
Wipe the screen after unlocking in a crowded place.
Use a six-digit PIN where the phone allows it.
Keep a second unlock method ready in case a finger is wet or cut.
Note the PIN nowhere on the device, including a note app.
Tell one trusted person at home where the PIN is written, sealed.

body.text: Lock the laptop too

items: On Windows, press the Windows key and L together, which locks immediately.
On a Mac, press Control, Command and Q.
Open Settings, then Accounts, then Sign-in options, to set a PIN for the laptop.
Set the screen to turn off after five minutes and require a sign-in.
Close the lid when you stand up, which locks on most machines by default.
Never leave a laptop open and signed in at a business centre.

body.text: The lock screen will show on the laptop within a second, and the desktop disappears behind it. That single key combination is worth learning by heart.

body.alt: A laptop showing the lock screen with a password field.
body.caption: Windows key and L locks a Windows laptop in one second. Nothing on the screen stays visible.

body.text: None of this slows your work. Unlocking takes one second, and it removes the risk of a stranger reading your email while you buy a drink.
Shared machines and other people's phones

items: On a shared computer, sign out of websites rather than only closing the tab.
Do not save the browser password on a machine you do not own.
Use a guest account when a visitor needs to check something.
On another person's phone, avoid opening your email, which stays signed in.
If you must use one, clear the session in the app before handing it back.
Change a password the moment you suspect somebody watched you type it.

body.text: Do not worry about being rude by locking a screen in front of a colleague. People who handle money and records do it without thinking.
If it goes wrong
Every case here has a route back, and none of them needs a new device.

items: You forgot the PIN: use the account recovery on the phone, which needs your Google or Apple password.
The fingerprint stops working: wash and dry the finger, then re-add it in Settings.
The phone locks too quickly: change the timeout to one minute.
A child changed the PIN: recovery through the parent account is the only route.
The laptop asks for a password you never set: it wants the Microsoft account password.
Facial unlock fails in the dark: type the PIN instead, which always works.

body.text: Practice
Set one lock today and the habit follows.

items: Set a six-digit PIN on the phone.
Lock and unlock it three times.
Press Windows and L on the laptop and sign back in.
Set the screen timeout to five minutes.
Tell one person at home where the PIN is written, in a sealed envelope.

body.text: You can now leave a device on a desk without worry. In the next lesson you will know exactly what to do in the first hour if a phone is stolen.

excerpt: The first hour after a phone is taken: block the SIM, lock the device remotely, change the important passwords, and report it in the right order.

body.text: This lesson tells you what to do if a phone is stolen, in the order that matters. You will block the SIM, lock the device from another screen, change the passwords that matter, and report the theft. The first hour is the one that counts.
A stolen phone is not only a lost device. It is a way into your messages, your bank alerts, and your accounts. Acting quickly closes those doors in a few minutes.
Before you start

items: Another phone, or a friend's phone, or a computer.
Your phone number and the name on the SIM registration.
Your Google or Apple account password, which you should know by heart.

body.text: The first fifteen minutes

items: Call your network provider and ask them to block the SIM and the line.
Ask for a replacement SIM with the same number, which usually takes a day.
From any computer, sign in to your Google or Apple account and choose Find my device.
Set the phone to lock remotely, and note its last location if one is shown.
Do not erase it yet. An erased phone cannot be located, and a locked one can.
Write down the time of each call, since the network will ask for it.

body.text: You will see the device listed in your account with its last seen time and a short list of actions. Lock, ring, and erase appear as buttons, and each one takes effect when the phone next reaches a network.

body.alt: A phone showing the find my device screen with a map and action buttons.
body.caption: Lock first, erase later. A locked phone is still findable, and an erased one is not.

body.text: It looks like erasing the phone is the safest first move. Erasing removes your data and also removes any chance of the police or the network tracing it.
Change these passwords, in this order

items: Email first, because every other reset arrives there.
Then the bank app, and call the bank to report the phone number.
Then WhatsApp, which needs a code sent to the number the thief now holds.
Then any account with money attached, such as a betting or wallet app.
Then social accounts, which are often used to message your contacts for money.
Change these from a computer, not from a phone you do not own.

body.text: None of this needs the old phone. Every one of these accounts can be recovered with the email address and a password you know.

body.alt: A list of devices signed in to an account with the option to sign each one out.
body.caption: Sign out every device you do not recognise. That closes the door even if the phone stays with the thief.

body.text: Report it properly

items: Report at the nearest police station and ask for a written report with a reference number.
Give the IMEI number, which is on the box or the receipt, and helps identify the handset.
Take a copy of the report, which the bank and the network will ask for.
Report the theft to your network provider, who can block the handset as well as the SIM.
Tell your close contacts that messages from your old number are not yours.
Ask the bank to send alerts by email rather than by text for a while.

body.text: Do not worry about the cost of a replacement yet. Sorting the accounts is the urgent part, and the phone can wait a week.
If it goes wrong
Every case here has a next step, and the first is the most common.

items: The find-device page shows the phone as offline: it will act when the phone next connects, so leave the lock request in place.
You cannot receive the WhatsApp code: wait for the SMS block to clear, or ask WhatsApp to send the code by call.
The bank says it needs the police report: get the report first, then return.
Your email password was also on the phone: recover the email through the backup address, and be ready for a delay.
A friend sends money to the thief: tell them to report it at once, since transfers can sometimes be reversed.
The thief photographs the SIM: blocking the line is the only fix, so call the network first.

body.text: Practice
Set this up today, while nothing is wrong.

items: Write your IMEI number on paper and keep it at home.
Sign in to your account from a computer and confirm the device is listed.
Check that you know your email password without looking it up.
Note your network provider's customer line in a paper address book.
Ask one family member to be the person you call first.

body.text: You now have a plan instead of panic. In the next lesson you will silence notifications without turning the phone off.

excerpt: How to silence calls and notifications for a set time, let one or two important people through, and be sure nothing important is missed.

body.text: This lesson teaches you to use Do Not Disturb so a phone stops buzzing without being switched off. You will set it for an hour, let one important contact through, and schedule it for the night.
Do Not Disturb silences notifications and calls for a set period. Alarms still ring, and the phone still takes messages, which arrive quietly and wait for you.
Before you start

items: A phone with notifications switched on.
About ten minutes.

body.text: Turn it on for an hour

items: Swipe down from the top of the screen to open quick settings.
Tap the crescent moon symbol, which is Do Not Disturb.
Look for the small moon in the status bar, which confirms it is on.
Send yourself a test message from another phone, or ask somebody to call.
The screen stays dark and no sound plays.
Tap the symbol again to switch it off.

body.text: You will see the moon icon beside the battery and the network bars. Notifications still arrive in the shade, so nothing is lost while the phone stays silent.

body.alt: A phone quick settings panel with the Do Not Disturb moon icon enabled.
body.caption: The crescent moon is the whole switch. The icon in the status bar tells you it is working.

body.text: It looks like silencing the phone means missing an emergency. You can let chosen contacts through, which is the setting most people never find.
Let the important calls through

items: Open Settings, then Sound, then Do Not Disturb.
Choose Calls and allow calls from starred or favourite contacts.
Turn on repeat calls, which lets a second call within fifteen minutes ring.
That last setting is the one that catches emergencies, because people call twice.
Add family numbers to favourites so they pass through.
Leave unknown numbers blocked, which is most of the noise.

body.text: A call from a favourite contact will now ring with sound, and the screen lights up as normal. Everything else stays quiet.

The screen will light up with the caller's name and a green answer button, even though everything else stays dark. A crescent moon appears at the corner of the notification shade, reminding you why the phone is silent.

body.alt: A phone face down on a desk during a work session.
body.caption: Face down and silent for an hour. A second call from the same number still comes through.

body.text: Schedule it for the night
The scheduled version is the one that improves sleep, because nobody remembers to switch it on at eleven.

items: In the same settings screen, choose Add schedule or Turn on as scheduled.
Set it from 22:00 to 06:00, or whatever matches your household.
Allow alarms, which is a separate switch and should stay on.
Allow favourite contacts, as above.
Check the schedule before a night when you expect an important call.
Switch the schedule off temporarily rather than deleting it.

body.text: None of this turns the phone off, so your alarm still rings and updates still download. Only the interruptions stop.
Do not worry about messages piling up. They arrive quietly in the notification shade, and the count waits for you.
If it goes wrong
Every case here is a setting, and the phone can always be returned to normal.

items: Calls do not ring at all: the exception list is empty. Add your favourites.
The alarm did not ring: alarms were switched off inside Do Not Disturb.
The phone still buzzes: another app has a bypass permission. Remove it in the app's settings.
You missed a delivery call: turn on repeat calls, or add the driver's number for the day.
Do Not Disturb will not switch off: a schedule is active. Turn the schedule off.
Nobody can reach you for a whole day: check the moon icon before you leave the house.

body.text: Practice
One silent hour, one important call allowed through, and the setting makes sense.

items: Turn Do Not Disturb on and confirm the moon icon.
Ask somebody to call and note that nothing rings.
Add that person to favourites and try again.
Set a nightly schedule for the hours you sleep.
Switch it off and confirm the icon disappears.

body.text: You can now protect your attention without going off the grid. In the next lesson you will turn a phone into a wifi hotspot for a laptop.

excerpt: How to share a phone's data with a laptop, set a real password, watch what it costs, and fix a laptop that keeps dropping off.

body.text: This lesson teaches you to use a phone as a hotspot, which lets a laptop use the phone's data. You will turn it on, set a proper password, connect the laptop, and keep an eye on what it costs.
A hotspot is the phone acting as a small wifi router. Other devices connect to it with a password and use the mobile data in the phone's SIM.
Before you start

items: A phone with data and a charged battery.
The laptop you want to connect.
A data plan you know the size of.

body.text: Turn it on

items: Open Settings, then Network, then Hotspot and tethering.
Tap Portable hotspot or Personal hotspot.
Change the hotspot name to something you recognise, such as your first name and phone.
Set the password to at least eight characters, mixing letters and numbers.
Turn on the hotspot and note the name it broadcasts.
Keep the phone where the signal is strongest, usually near a window.

body.text: You will see a small hotspot icon appear in the status bar, often a chain link or a curved signal, and the phone gets warm within a few minutes.

body.alt: A phone hotspot settings screen showing the network name and password.
body.caption: Set your own name and password before anything connects. The default password is often short and printed on the box.

body.text: It looks like the hotspot is free once the data is paid for. It uses the same data as the phone, and a laptop can spend a month's bundle in an afternoon of video.
Connect the laptop

items: Click the wifi symbol in the bottom-right corner of the laptop screen.
Find the hotspot name in the list and click it.
Type the password exactly, watching the capital letters.
Choose yes when the laptop asks whether this is a trusted network.
Open a page to confirm the connection works.
Turn the hotspot off when you finish, which stops the battery draining.

body.text: The laptop will show the network as connected, with a wifi symbol and the name underneath. If it shows Connected but no internet, the phone's data or the signal is the problem.

body.alt: A laptop wifi list showing a phone hotspot network and a connected state.
body.caption: The hotspot appears in the laptop's wifi list like any other network. The password on the phone is the one it needs.

body.text: Keeping the cost down

items: Set a data limit in the hotspot settings, so the phone warns you at a chosen size.
Turn on the laptop's data saver, which reduces background use.
Pause cloud sync and automatic updates while you are on the hotspot.
Close video tabs, which use far more than documents and email.
Use the hotspot for one task at a time rather than leaving it on all evening.
Check the data counter afterwards, since it tells you plainly what the session cost.

body.text: None of this needs a special plan on most networks. The data comes from the bundle already on the SIM.
Do not worry if the phone gets warm. A hotspot runs the radio hard, and the heat is expected while it works.
If it goes wrong
Every case here is a setting or a signal, and the connection comes back.

items: The hotspot does not appear in the laptop list: turn it off and on again, then refresh the list.
The password is rejected: check capital letters, and read it from the phone screen.
Connected but no internet: mobile data is off, or the bundle is finished.
The laptop drops every few minutes: the phone is sleeping. Keep the screen on, or plug it in.
The hotspot name has changed on its own: the network reset the settings. Set it again.
The battery empties in an hour: tethering is heavy. Charge the phone while it works.

body.text: Practice
One session, watched carefully, teaches more than the settings do.

items: Set the hotspot name and an eight-character password.
Turn it on and connect the laptop.
Open one page and confirm it loads.
Check the data counter before and after.
Turn the hotspot off and note the battery change.

body.text: You can now get a laptop online anywhere with a signal. In the next lesson you will see which connection a phone is using, and which one is quietly costing money.

excerpt: How to tell whether a phone is on wifi or mobile data, how to switch between them on purpose, and the settings that stop data disappearing.

body.text: This lesson teaches you to tell whether a phone is using wifi or mobile data, and how to choose. You will read the icons, switch between the two, and stop apps from spending data in the background.
Wifi comes from a router and costs nothing per gigabyte. Mobile data comes from the network and comes out of your bundle. Both can be on at once, and the phone decides which to use.
Before you start

items: A phone with both a SIM and a wifi network nearby.
About ten minutes.

body.text: Read the icons

items: A fan or curved-triangle symbol means wifi is connected and in use.
A row of bars with 4G, LTE, or 5G beside it means mobile data is available.
Small arrows under the bars mean data is moving up or down right now.
An exclamation mark beside the wifi symbol means connected but no internet.
A plane symbol means every radio is off, so nothing connects.
Swipe down to see the full panel, where both toggles are visible.

body.text: You will see the top bar change within a second when you switch, and the wifi fan disappears as the data arrows take over.

body.alt: A phone status bar showing a wifi icon and mobile data bars side by side.
body.caption: A fan means wifi. Bars with 4G mean data. When wifi is connected, the phone prefers it and stops using data.

body.text: It looks like mobile data is off whenever wifi is connected. It stays on in the background, ready to take over the moment wifi drops, which is where bundles disappear.
Switch on purpose

items: Swipe down and tap the wifi symbol to turn wifi on or off.
Tap the mobile data symbol to do the same for the network.
Turn mobile data off when you are on wifi for the day, if the signal is reliable.
Turn wifi off when the network is a weak public one, since it drains the battery.
Forget a public network when you leave, so the phone stops trying.
Set a data warning in Settings, then Mobile network, then Data warning.

body.text: The data toggle turns a different colour when it is off, which is the fastest way to check before handing a phone to a child.

body.alt: A phone quick settings panel showing separate wifi and mobile data toggles.
body.caption: Two separate switches. Turning data off does not turn wifi off, and the reverse is also true.

body.text: Stop the quiet spending
Most bundle loss happens without anybody opening an app. The fixes are all in one place.
The data usage screen will show every app, largest first, with the month's total at the top. Beside each app name a small figure appears with the amount it used, which is where the answer usually is.

items: Open Settings, then Apps, then each large app, and restrict background data.
In the Play Store, set app updates to wifi only.
In WhatsApp, turn off automatic media download, which is often the largest single saving.
Turn on data saver, which tells apps to use less and wait for wifi.
Check the data usage screen, which lists apps from largest to smallest.
Set the monthly cycle date correctly, or the counter resets on the wrong day.

body.text: None of these stop the apps working. They delay the heavy parts until wifi is available.
Do not worry about watching every megabyte. Three settings cover most of the waste, and the counter does the rest.
Public wifi and the tap you trust

items: Treat a cafe or hotel network as public, because other people share it.
Avoid banking on public wifi, and use mobile data instead for that task.
Check the network name with the staff, since copycat names are common.
Turn off file sharing and nearby sharing while you are on it.
Sign out of accounts you opened on a shared network.
Turn wifi off when you leave, so the phone does not reconnect on its own.

body.text: If it goes wrong
Every case here has a plain explanation and a short fix.

items: Wifi says connected but pages will not load: the router has no internet. Use data.
Data is on but nothing loads: the bundle is finished, or the network is weak.
The phone keeps choosing wifi over data: that is the default, and it is usually right.
The data counter shows more than the network says: some apps count differently, so check the network's own figure.
The wifi keeps dropping: move closer to the router, or forget and rejoin.
Both icons are missing: airplane mode is on.

body.text: Practice
Read the bar, flip both switches, and the phone stops being a mystery.

items: Note which icon is showing now and what it means.
Turn mobile data off and load a page on wifi.
Turn wifi off and load the same page on data.
Open the data usage screen and find the largest app.
Restrict background data for that app.

body.text: You can now see which tap is open and close it when you choose. In the next lesson you will photograph a document so the words come out readable.
